response.sql:
WITH scan_rates AS (
  SELECT s.healtheval, sc.scancount, sc.gbsize::double precision / NULLIF(sc.spanmin, 0)::double precision AS gb_per_min
  FROM scans sc
  JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
),
status_rates AS (
  SELECT healtheval AS status, SUM(scancount) AS total_scancount, AVG(gb_per_min) AS rate
  FROM scan_rates
  GROUP BY healtheval
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM status_rates
)
SELECT r.status, r.total_scancount, r.rate, r.rate - o.avg_rate AS rate_minus_avg
FROM status_rates r
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE r.rate > o.avg_rate

assumptions.assumption: Database is PostgreSQL; the cast to double precision avoids the precision loss of REAL division so the rate is not rounded.
Scans with no matching site (inner join on zoneref = zoneregistry) are dropped, as the request says.
A spanmin of 0 is treated as missing (NULLIF), so that scan's ratio is ignored instead of raising a division-by-zero error.
Sites with a NULL healtheval form their own status group, because GROUP BY treats NULL as a group.
The average across statuses is an unweighted mean of the per-status rates; statuses whose rate is NULL are ignored, and if no status has a rate the comparison yields no rows.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude scans whose site has a NULL health and safety status, so no NULL status group appears in the output or in the cross-status average.

WITH scan_rates AS (
  SELECT s.healtheval, sc.scancount, sc.gbsize::double precision / NULLIF(sc.spanmin, 0)::double precision AS gb_per_min
  FROM scans sc
  JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
  WHERE s.healtheval IS NOT NULL
),
status_rates AS (
  SELECT healtheval AS status, SUM(scancount) AS total_scancount, AVG(gb_per_min) AS rate
  FROM scan_rates
  GROUP BY healtheval
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM status_rates
)
SELECT r.status, r.total_scancount, r.rate, r.rate - o.avg_rate AS rate_minus_avg
FROM status_rates r
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE r.rate > o.avg_rate
